Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"

## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)

When choosing a `prefix_rule`, request one that will allow you to fulfill similar requests from the user in the future without re-requesting escalation. It should be categorical and reasonably scoped to similar capabilities. You should rarely pass the entire command into `prefix_rule`.

NEVER provide a prefix_rule argument for destructive commands like rm.
NEVER provide a prefix_rule if your command uses a heredoc or herestring.

# -> 100% CPU + machine freeze (macOS "beachball"). tests/conftest.py defends on

# pytest_configure renices the pytest processes (os.nice) so the OS always
# preempts them for the UI. Overrides: PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS for worker

# stay on one worker.

    "--strict-config",
    "--timeout=120",
    "--timeout-method=thread",
    "-n",
    "logical",
    "--dist",
    "loadfile",
]

# (keep everything, retain 3 sessions) makes pytest rmtree three full
# pytest-of-<user> trees at startup — tens of thousands of fs events that feed
# the same launchservicesd/fseventsd storm the conftest isolation fixtures were
# reworked to avoid (see tests/conftest.py `_isolate_history_db`).

    "slow: marks tests as slow running (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "conformance: marks tests as host conformance tests (deselect with '-m \"not conformance\"')",

[project.entry-points."little_loops.extensions"]
# Extensions register here for automatic discovery.
# Example: my_ext = "my_package:MyExtension"

[project.entry-points.pytest11]
# ENH-2459: records pytest run results into .ll/history.db (test_run_events).
# Opt out with PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_LL_HISTORY=1 or `-p no:ll_history`.
ll_history = "little_loops.pytest_history_plugin"

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    # Upper bound is deliberate. The full suite began hanging at ~98-99%
    # completion under xdist (`-n logical --dist loadfile` +
    # `--timeout-method=thread`, see [tool.pytest.ini_options] below) once the
    # uncapped `>=7.0` pin started resolving to pytest 9.x against
    # pytest-xdist 3.8.0. Thread-method timeouts leave watchdog threads on
    # idle workers rather than terminating them (pytest-xdist #1094/#117,
    # pytest-timeout #72/#137), which is what wedges the run at the tail when
    # most workers have gone idle. Lift the cap only alongside a verified
    # clean full-suite run on the newer major.
    "pytest>=7.0,<9",
    "pytest-cov>=4.0",
    # BUG-3208 had two halves: pytest 9.x AND pytest-xdist 3.8.0 interact to
    # trigger the thread-method watchdog leak on idle workers (same root
    # cause as the pytest<9 cap above: xdist issue #1094/#117 + timeout #72/#137).
    # The pytest<9 cap is in place, but xdist<3.8 is also required — a fresh
    # venv still resolves `pytest-xdist>=3.0` to 3.8.0 (the BUG-3208-stamped
    # version) and repros the wedge on pytest 8.x with the same addopts.
    # Lift only alongside a verified clean full-suite run on the newer xdist.
    "pytest-xdist>=3.0,<3.8",
    # psutil moved to [project].dependencies (FEAT-2930) — it now backs both
    # xdist's `-n logical` core detection and _reclaim_stale's PID-liveness
    # identity check, so it's no longer dev-only.
    "pytest-timeout>=2.0",
    "hypothesis>=6.0",
    "mutmut>=3.0",
    # Pinned (not >=): an unpinned ruff let formatting drift between
    # contributor machines, surfacing as a ~50-file reformat on unrelated
    # branches. Bump deliberately, in the same commit as a full reformat.
    "ruff==0.14.10",
    "mypy>=1.0",
    "hatch>=1.0",
    "syrupy>=4.0",
    "pre-commit>=3.0",
]
llm = []
# FEAT-3135: exact pin, not a range. The 1.x line does not implement the
# 2026-07-28 no-`initialize`-handshake behavior `ll-mcp` is built on
# (proven: .ll/learning-tests/mcp.md, installed 1.21.0 rejects it), and
# 2.0.0 is the first and only 2.x release — there is no 2.x track record to
# justify an open upper bound. Optional rather than base because mcp==2.0.0
# pulls 16 mandatory transitive deps including a full HTTP server stack
# (starlette, uvicorn, sse-starlette, httpx2), pyjwt[crypto],
# opentelemetry-api, python-multipart, and jsonschema. `ll-mcp` now uses the
# HTTP server stack directly for its streamable-HTTP transport (FEAT-3143,
# `run_http()`), so those pieces are no longer merely transitive baggage —
# but they still land on every `pip install little-loops[mcp]` regardless of
# whether a given install ever runs `ll-mcp --http`, which is why this stays
# an optional extra rather than a base dependency. Per CLAUDE.md § Code Style
# (minimize third-party dependencies).
mcp = ["mcp==2.0.0"]
otel = [
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.20.0",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-grpc>=1.20.0",
]
webhooks = [
    "httpx>=0.24.0",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["little_loops"]
include = ["little_loops/**", "LICENSE", "README.md"]

# BUG-3177: skills/ stays physically at the repo root (host-plugin glue,
# FEAT-2274/BUG-938's deliberate out-of-wheel boundary) but ll-mcp's
# prompts-from-skills surface (FEAT-3137) is package code that now genuinely
# reads it, so a build-time copy lands in the wheel without relocating the
# source tree or touching .claude-plugin/plugin.json's "./skills" reference.
#
# This is a custom build hook (hatch_build.py), not a static force-include table,
# because a static "../skills" mapping is required in both the wheel and sdist
# targets (a PyPI release also publishes an sdist, and `pip install` from source
# builds the wheel *from the sdist's contents*) — but building the wheel from an
# already-unpacked sdist has no "../skills" to find (the sdist already copied it
# in-place at little_loops/skills/), and hatchling's force-include hard-fails on a
# missing source rather than skipping it. See hatch_build.py's docstring.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.hooks.custom]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist.hooks.custom]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "UP", "B", "C4"]
ignore = ["E501"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
# Coverage is intentionally NOT in addopts: instrumentation adds ~30-100%
# overhead on every run. For a coverage report use the opt-in invocation:
#   python -m pytest scripts/tests/ --cov=little_loops \
#       --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered --cov-report=html
# (the [tool.coverage.*] config below still applies when --cov is passed.)
# -n logical runs xdist across logical CPUs. The raw logical count would spawn
# one worker per core (e.g. 14/14 on Apple Silicon, where logical == physical
# since there is no SMT), saturating every core and starving the OS compositor
# -> 100% CPU + machine freeze (macOS "beachball"). tests/conftest.py defends on
# two axes: pytest_xdist_auto_num_workers caps workers to ~half the cores, and
# pytest_configure renices the pytest processes (os.nice) so the OS always
# preempts them for the UI. Overrides: PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS for worker
# count, LL_TEST_NO_NICE=1 to skip the renice, -n 0 to force serial (pdb).
# --timeout=120 is a per-test safety net: any test that hangs past 120s is
# killed and reported as a timeout, freeing the xdist worker slot before it
# can wedge a core indefinitely. Tests with legitimately slow wall-clock
# can opt out via @pytest.mark.timeout(N) per test.
# --timeout-method=thread is explicit because signal-based timeouts race
# with xdist worker process management.
# --dist loadfile gives each test file worker affinity: far fewer
# controller<->worker scheduling round-trips than the default per-test `load`
# on a ~13.7k-test suite, and per-file fixtures (git repos, subprocess envs)
# stay on one worker.
addopts = [
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "--timeout=120",
    "--timeout-method=thread",
    "-n",
    "logical",
    "--dist",
    "loadfile",
]
# Keep only failed-test tmp dirs, and only the last session's tree. The default
# (keep everything, retain 3 sessions) makes pytest rmtree three full
# pytest-of-<user> trees at startup — tens of thousands of fs events that feed
# the same launchservicesd/fseventsd storm the conftest isolation fixtures were
# reworked to avoid (see tests/conftest.py `_isolate_history_db`).
tmp_path_retention_count = 1
tmp_path_retention_policy = "failed"
markers = [
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests (deselect with '-m \"not integration\"')",
    "slow: marks tests as slow running (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "conformance: marks tests as host conformance tests (deselect with '-m \"not conformance\"')",
    "no_parallel: marks tests that must not run on xdist workers (subprocess signal-handling, timing-sensitive). Under the default -n logical addopts this SKIPS the test outright (the controller never runs tests under -n N); it only actually runs in a serial -n 0 invocation — see scripts/tests/conftest.py",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["little_loops"]
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/__init__.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
]
fail_under = 80

[tool.mutmut]
paths_to_mutate = ["little_loops/"]
pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection = ["tests/"]
# -n0 disables xdist for per-mutant runs: each mutant runs a tiny test subset,
# so worker spawn overhead would outweigh any parallelism gain.
pytest_add_cli_args = ["-x", "-q", "-n0"]
